column3: *** THE FIRST CONSTITUTIONAL PRESIDENT OF URUGUAY AND THE FIRST LADY, AT THE FONT FOR SANCHO LLERENA'S GRANDSON. *** Rivera was president from 1830 to 1834; the act is of December 1831, squarely in his first term.

column1: # *** WHAT THIS CHANGES. ***
# This archive has carried the Lerenas as obscure - "naturales del E. Oriental" in a Rosario act, a
# hacendado's death in 1901, a tinsmith wrongly thought to be one of them. The social picture was
# thin and mostly inferred.
# It is not thin. In December 1831 the President of the Republic and his wife stood as godparents to
# a grandson of Sancho Llerena. Padrinos of that rank are not chosen at random: they mark a family
# with standing, or a debt, or a connection to the Rivera circle. *** That is a research direction
# this archive has never had. ***
# It also fits what came later: Justiniana's father was a GENERAL; Candido Juanico was an ABOGADO;
# Luis Eugenio died a HACENDADO; Ema Sixta married the philosopher Jose Pedro Massera; Candido Jaime
# married a Magarinos. *** The pattern is consistent, and it starts earlier than anything here. ***
# AND A CAUTION, because the temptation is obvious. Nothing in this act touches Pablo Armando or
# Juan Carlos. It is about the generation of Sancho's children, sixty years earlier, and it is
# recorded as social context and a new sibling - not as descent.
